Whether one goes to AA and follows in their footsteps is a choice, and it’s a personal one for all problem drinkers. Surely there are pluses and minuses, IMO, the plus side of the ledger is much fuller though.

I was raised in a manner that made me very angry at God, and truly despised people who went to church, viewing them as hypocrites, and generally as assholes. When people would mention God, I became very angry and self righteous and would start looking at them as flawed in a major way.

For some reason.......I couldn’t stay sober though....ya, I would get a month here or there, sometimes life would get a little better, then I would find myself in even worse shape than before.

Life, my alcoholism and my pride finally had a showdown where I admitted I was done fighting.

Whether my willingness to believe in a power greater than myself was merely a manifestation of me being completely done, or whether it was the key to unlock a better way of life? I truly don’t know. Does it matter?

After having spent years being homeless, or very close to it, and having jobs through a lot of this time, to finally be able to live like a ‘normal’ person was a miracle.

For my higher power? I truly don’t know still....I am very intrigued by many of the gnostic writings that were not included in the Bible, thinking somewhere in there, was a truth that was hidden right in plain sight.

Today, after seven years, I try to maintain a true sense of gratitude, and know that to make my life a living hell, it would just take one drink, and I have been tempted many times, and thankfully have not done so.

AA is wonderful for the support group it offers, if you go to them, just try and not be like me, and try to not be so oppositional to the concept of God. I don’t know, but it seemed to me it was more important for me to be right, than sober.

It was only when I realized I couldn’t have both that I was willing to look at the idea I may have been wrong.

I am NOT saying everyone would have that same experience as me, just saying how it was for me. Regardless of how your journey treats you? Know I’m on your side, no matter what path you try.
Thanks for taking the time to write this out, I appreciate it. And congrats on your success
